findings.summary: Regression from 1.0.0. Long-form listing cards lost their plates. In 1.0.0 (and in 1.1.0-rc.1) every post card on the home grid and under 'Related posts' had a plate with the post's own drawing. In this sample both grids are text-only cards, so the listing pages carry only one featured stage and a header drawing. The agent reports why: 'The data has no images, so there was nothing missing to replace with a drawing.' The spec allows that reading. The Imagery rule now begins 'Missing images: first ask what the image is for' and only applies when an image is missing. The Card grid row ('plates with photos or the item's own drawing, one per card') and the Long-form row ('plates') do not say whether a card whose data has no image field counts as missing one. The reference does use text-only resource cards (p3 'Get the technical rundown', p6 'Technical resources'), so this is not off-reference. It is still clearly less of the system's signature than the published version showed on the same kind of screen.
findings.promptFix: State when a card gets an image regardless of the data. 'A grid of items that each have their own subject (entries, products, places, people's work) shows a plate per card even when the data has no image field: the item's own drawing, the same one on its detail page. The missing-image rules decide what goes on the plate, not whether there is one. Text-only cards are for link lists, resources and metadata rows.' Add to Verification: 'Every card grid of subject items has a plate on every card.'

findings.summary: Two drawings fail the one-word test. The sweater plate, reused on its detail stage, is a folded slab with a neckline arc, held from below. It reads as a box or a clutch, not a sweater (1.0.0 drew a whole sweater). The article header's reading glasses, temples raised, read as the letters '6d'. The reference's small objects read at once.

The inventory-board ghosted preview is one short row of six tiles inside a thin raised card. It fills about a fifth of the stage's height, so the lilac media stage reads mostly empty. The release-notes comparison figure fills its stage properly.

notes: Update goal (the two rc.1 regressions). Both are reached in this sample. (1) Information figures are now ghosted previews on media stages, shaped like their captions: a grid of grouped tiles for the inventory board, and two side-by-side panels with one ink bar for the 'same release, two audiences' comparison. No pictogram stands in for a structure (blog posts-*-desktop-light, compared with rc.1's button and pencil). (2) At 390px the four short metric cards sit 2x2 again (dashboard home-mobile-light). The rest of the generalization still holds: header drawing and write-in h1 on every product screen, the primary chart on one stage, the transaction summary in a side column, a stable plate color per item, offer cards on a stage that stack fully at 390px (settings-billing-mobile-light). The new major is a side effect of the same missing-image rewrite: listing cards lost their plates.

Earlier verdict (rc.1 critic-1). Its two majors are fixed (see above). Nothing else regressed apart from the plate finding. The rc.1 minor about the 90px gap on the item detail screen does not recur (projects-apollo-migration-desktop-light). The rc.1 minor about the working glyph sitting beside 'Refreshing…' recurs (state-loading-desktop-light) and is not re-raised. The tea-towel plate now has a stripe band and a hanging loop and reads better than in rc.1 (commerce home-d9).
Measured layout defects: none listed. Harness capture artifact, not counted: the dialog scrim ends at 900px in the full-page capture (settings state-plan-dialog-desktop-light).
Gates: all passed on all four apps. Smoke tests were not run for this screen; they run at the confirm step.

Reference fidelity 4. Cream paper and warm ink, a serif display over a quiet sans, pastel stages crossed by faint wandering lines, ink ring controls, and stepped cel drawings that hold (blog motion-m2, settings motion-settings-billing-m2). Compared with reference p1/p3: the same calm, airy section rhythm. Nothing is copied.

Signature 3.5. All elements are present in all four apps. Motion steps in stroke by stroke and holds. The hands come from several edges in different poses. Held down by the lost listing plates (major) and two weak drawings (minor). Hierarchy 4: serif h1 plus drawing, then one stage or main card on every screen. Component states 4: clay focus rings, danger rings with inline messages and an 'N fields need attention' line, a designed dialog, an empty state with a drawing and one action, skeletons. Cross-app 4: one family in light and dark (commerce home-mobile-dark, dashboard team-desktop-dark, settings-notifications-desktop-dark). Polish 4: no browser-default leftovers.
